title: Anatomy of an Ottoman Mosque
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Hover over nine numbered parts of an Ottoman mosque and its courtyard, in the order a visitor meets them, to learn what each is for and what a respectful visitor does there, then test yourself in Quiz mode.

learningObjectives: The learner will name nine parts of an Ottoman mosque and its courtyard in the order a visitor meets them, and say what each part is for and what a respectful visitor does there.
prerequisites: Daily prayer, ablution, the minaret, and the call to prayer, from [Chapter 5](../../chapters/05-ottoman-istanbul/index.md).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Interactive exploration followed by retrieval practice
keyQuestions: What does a respectful visitor do here?
commonMisconceptions: The minaret is where people pray inside.
Visitors can walk in wearing shoes and any clothing.
assessmentOpportunities: Quiz mode: identify each marked part from its description

controls.name: Explore
controls.description: Default mode: hover a marker or label to read about that part.

controls.name: Quiz
controls.description: Hides the labels and asks you to click the marker that matches each description.
